questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a listed indication for chemotherapy in breast cancer?
opts: T1 tumor with ER, PR +ve and low recurrence risk
questions.exp: Indications for chemotherapy: 1. +ve lymph nodes; 2. Locally advanced breast cancers; 3. ER, PR -ve tumors; 4. Her 2 neu +ve tumors; 5. metastasis. (Book p68)

questions.q: Chemotherapy is indicated for breast tumors that are:
questions.exp: Indication #3 for chemotherapy: ER, PR -ve tumors. (Book p68)

questions.q: Which is NOT an indication for neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT)?
opts: Small tumor with no desire for breast conservation
Large tumor with patient desiring BCS
questions.exp: NACT indications: 1. LABC; 2. TNBC; 3. HER 2 Neu +ve; 4. Large tumors with patient desiring Breast conservation Sx (BCS). (Book p68)

questions.q: NACT is indicated for large tumors when the patient desires:
questions.exp: NACT indication #4: Large tumors with patient desiring Breast conservation Sx (BCS). (Book p68)

questions.q: Which is an advantage of NACT?
opts: Remove the need for RT after BCS
questions.exp: Advantages of NACT: Downstage/downsize the tumour; ↓ micrometastasis; in vivo chemosensitivity indicator (RECIST criteria). (Book p68)

questions.q: NACT decreases which of the following?
questions.exp: Advantages of NACT include ↓ micrometastasis. (Book p68)

questions.q: The in vivo chemosensitivity indicator during NACT is assessed by:
questions.exp: In vivo chemosensitivity indicator: RECIST criteria (Response evaluation criteria in solid tumors). (Book p68)

questions.q: RECIST stands for:
opts: Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors
Response Estimation Criteria In Soft Tissues
Recurrence Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors
Response Evaluation Criteria In Skin Tumors
questions.exp: RECIST criteria = Response evaluation criteria in solid tumors. (Book p68)

questions.q: On RECIST, Complete Response (CR) means:
opts: Disappearance of all lesions & pathological lymph nodes
questions.exp: CR: Disappearance of all lesions & pathological lymph nodes. (Book p68)

questions.q: Which breast cancer subtype has the highest pathological CR (pCR) rates?
questions.exp: pCR: TNBC have highest pCR rates. (Book p68)

questions.q: Partial Response (PR) on RECIST requires at least what change in the single largest diameter (SLD)?
questions.exp: PR: ≥30% ↓ in single largest diameter (SLD), no new lesions, no progression of non target lesions. (Book p68)

questions.q: Which is required for a Partial Response (PR) on RECIST?
opts: No new lesions and no progression of non target lesions
questions.exp: PR: ≥30% ↓ SLD; No new lesions; No progression of non target lesions. (Book p68)

questions.q: Stable Disease (SD) on RECIST is defined as:
questions.exp: SD: No PR or PD. (Book p68)

questions.q: Progressive Disease (PD) on RECIST includes ≥20% increase in SLD, progression of non target lesions, or:
questions.exp: PD: ≥20% ↑ SLD (or) Progression of non target lesions (or) New lesions. (Book p68)

questions.q: A chemoport is placed:
questions.exp: Chemoport: Placed below the clavicle; used to deliver chemo drugs; prevents thrombophlebitis. (Book p69)

questions.q: On X-ray, the chemoport tip lies in:
questions.exp: X Ray chemoport: Tip lies in SVC just above right atrium. (Book p69)

questions.q: A chemoport prevents which complication of chemotherapy delivery?
questions.exp: Chemoport prevents thrombophlebitis. (Book p69)

questions.q: In the CAF/CMF regimens (now not used), F stands for:
questions.exp: CAF/CMF (not used): C cyclophosphamide, A Adriamycin, F 5-Fluorouracil, m methotrexate. (Book p69)

questions.q: In CMF, the letter m stands for:
questions.exp: m: methotrexate. (Book p69)

questions.q: In CAF, the letter A stands for:
questions.exp: A: Adriamycin. (Book p69)

questions.q: The currently used regimen for Her 2 neu -ve breast cancer is:
questions.exp: Her 2 neu -ve: Currently used = 4 cycles AC/EC then 4 cycles T. (Book p69)

questions.q: In the AC/EC regimen, E stands for:
questions.exp: E: Epirubicin. (Book p69)

questions.q: The T in '4 cycles T' refers to:
questions.exp: T: Taxanes (Paclitaxel/Docetaxel). (Book p69)

questions.q: The side effect of Paclitaxel is:
questions.exp: S/E of Paclitaxel: Peripheral neuropathy. (Book p69)

questions.q: The regimen for Her 2 neu +ve breast cancer is:
questions.exp: Her 2 neu +ve: 6 cycles TCH + P. (Book p69)

questions.q: In TCH + P, the C stands for:
questions.exp: TCH + P: T Taxanes, C Carboplatin, H Herceptin, P Pertuzumab. (Book p69)

questions.q: Which two drugs in TCH + P are the anti-Her 2 neu agents?
questions.exp: H: Herceptin + P: Pertuzumab = Anti-Her 2 neu. (Book p69)

questions.q: Chemotherapy is avoided in breast cancer patients with:
questions.exp: Avoid chemotherapy in: 1. Poor performance status (Karnofsky/ECOG score); 2. Low-risk molecular profile. (Book p69)

questions.q: In T1/T2, N0/N1, M0 with ER ± and Her 2 neu -ve disease, molecular testing is done to indicate:
questions.exp: For T1/T2, N0/N1, M0, ER±, Her2 neu- patients: Do molecular testing (indicates risk of recurrence). (Book p69)

questions.q: If molecular testing shows LOW risk of recurrence, the plan is:
questions.exp: Molecular testing: Low → Avoid chemo; High → Chemo given. (Book p69)

questions.q: Oncotype Dx is a:
questions.exp: Oncotype Dx: 21 gene assay. (Book p69)

questions.q: Mammaprint is a:
questions.exp: Mammaprint: 70 gene assay. (Book p69)

questions.q: Endopredict is a:
questions.exp: Endopredict: 12 gene assay. (Book p69)

questions.q: PAM 50 is a:
questions.exp: PAM 50: 50 gene assay. (Book p69)

questions.q: The Indian molecular test for recurrence risk in breast cancer is:
questions.exp: CAN assist: Indian test. (Book p69)

questions.q: Which is NOT a listed indication for radiotherapy in breast cancer?
opts: T1 tumor <2 cm with clear margins and N0
questions.exp: RT indications: 1. +ve lymph nodes; 2. Tumor >5 cm (> T3); 3. Locally advanced breast carcinoma (LABC); 4. After BCS. (Book p70)

questions.q: Whole breast irradiation (WBI) targets the breast and which lymph nodes?
questions.exp: WBI target sites: Breast + Lymph nodes: Axilla, infra & supraclavicular, internal mammary. (Book p70)

questions.q: The duration and dose of WBI is:
questions.exp: WBI duration: 25 days: 50-54 Gy. (Book p70)

questions.q: Accelerated partial breast irradiation (APBI) is delivered over:
questions.exp: APBI duration: 5 days: 30-34 Gy. (Book p70)

questions.q: The target site of APBI is:
questions.exp: APBI target: Partial breast. (Book p70)

questions.q: Which is NOT an indication of APBI?
questions.exp: APBI indications: 1. T1; 2. ER, PR (+); 3. -ve lymphovascular invasion; 4. Unifocal; 5. -ve margins; 6. ≥50 years. (Book p70)

questions.q: In APBI, the electrodes are placed in:
questions.exp: APBI: Electrodes placed in cavity. (Book p70)

questions.q: Hormonal therapy in breast cancer is indicated when:
opts: Only when both ER and PR are +ve
questions.exp: Hormonal therapy indication: Either or both ER/PR +ve. (Book p70)

questions.q: The drug for pre-menopausal women is:
questions.exp: Pre-menopausal: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM): Tamoxifen. (Book p70)

questions.q: Tamoxifen belongs to which drug class?
questions.exp: Tamoxifen = SERM. (Book p70)

questions.q: The drugs for post-menopausal women are:
questions.exp: Post-menopausal: Aromatase inhibitors: Letrozole, Anastrozole. (Book p70)

questions.q: The standard duration of tamoxifen is:
opts: 5 years (extended upto 10 years in some cases)
questions.exp: Tamoxifen duration: 5 years; in some cases extended upto 10 years. (Book p70)

questions.q: The duration of aromatase inhibitor therapy is:
questions.exp: Aromatase inhibitors duration: 5-10 years. (Book p70)

questions.q: The most common side effect of tamoxifen is:
questions.exp: Tamoxifen side effects: Hot flashes (m/c), endometrial hyperplasia, DVT. (Book p70)

questions.q: Besides hot flashes, tamoxifen causes:
questions.exp: Tamoxifen S/E: Hot flashes (m/c); Endometrial hyperplasia; DVT. (Book p70)

questions.q: The most common side effect of aromatase inhibitors is:
questions.exp: Aromatase inhibitors: Osteoporosis (m/c). (Book p70)

questions.exp: Before starting aromatase inhibitors, baseline DEXA scan done. If low, start vit D3, Ca2+ & bisphosphonate. (Book p70)

questions.q: If the DEXA scan is low before starting aromatase inhibitors, start:
questions.exp: If DEXA low: start vit D3, Ca2+ & bisphosphonate. (Book p70)

questions.q: When planning pregnancy while on tamoxifen, tamoxifen must be completely taken for how many years (out of 5)?
questions.exp: Tamoxifen has to be completely taken for 2 years (out of 5 years) before pausing for pregnancy. (Book p70)

questions.q: If a patient on tamoxifen wants to conceive after 2 years (no distant mets/contraindication), tamoxifen must be stopped:
questions.exp: Tamoxifen has to be stopped 3 months prior to conception. (Book p70)

questions.q: The most important prognostic factor in breast cancer is:
questions.exp: Most important prognostic factor: Axillary LN status. (Book p71)

questions.q: In metastatic breast cancer, the most important prognostic factor is:
questions.exp: In metastatic breast cancer: ER, PR status. (Book p71)

questions.q: Which is a poor prognostic DISEASE factor?

questions.exp: Aggressive biology: Her2/neu positive and triple negative. (Book p71)

questions.q: Which is a poor prognostic PATIENT factor?

questions.q: Between 2-5 years, follow-up visits are:
questions.exp: Every 6 months b/w 2-5 years. (Book p71)

questions.q: After 5 years, follow-up visits are:

questions.q: Metastatic breast cancer is defined by:

questions.exp: Mx of metastatic disease: Palliative. (Book p72)

questions.q: In metastatic breast cancer, Olaparib is used if:
questions.exp: Olaparib is used if BRCA +ve. (Book p72)

Only the larger one is staged

questions.exp: Obesity, alcohol intake, liver cirrhosis (with Klinefelter). (Book p73)

questions.exp: Comedo: ER, PR -ve; Presents as a lump. (Book p73)

units.title: Chemotherapy Indications & NACT
units.guide: Chemo is for +ve nodes, locally advanced disease, ER/PR -ve, Her2 +ve and metastasis; NACT is for LABC, TNBC, HER2 +ve and large tumors wanting BCS - it downstages, cuts micrometastasis and gives an in vivo chemosensitivity readout.

units.title: RECIST Criteria
units.guide: RECIST grades response in solid tumors: CR wipes out all lesions and pathological nodes, pCR is highest in TNBC, PR needs ≥30% fall in single largest diameter with no new/progressing lesions, SD is neither PR nor PD, and PD is ≥20% rise, progression or new lesions.

units.title: Chemoport & Regimens
units.guide: The chemoport sits below the clavicle with its tip in the SVC just above the right atrium, sparing veins from thrombophlebitis. Old CAF/CMF is retired; Her2 -ve gets 4 cycles AC/EC then 4 cycles T (paclitaxel causes peripheral neuropathy), Her2 +ve gets 6 cycles TCH + P with Herceptin and Pertuzumab as the anti-Her2 duo.

units.title: Avoiding Chemo & Molecular Tests
units.guide: Skip chemo in poor performance status and low-risk molecular profiles (T1/T2, N0/N1, M0, ER±, Her2 -ve). The assays: Oncotype Dx 21 genes, Mammaprint 70, Endopredict 12, PAM 50 fifty, and CAN assist is the Indian test; low risk avoids chemo, high risk gets it.

units.title: Radiotherapy: WBI vs APBI
units.guide: RT follows BCS always and covers +ve nodes, >5 cm tumors and LABC. WBI bathes breast plus axillary, infra/supraclavicular and internal mammary nodes over 25 days (50-54 Gy); APBI shrinks this to partial breast, 5 days (30-34 Gy) with cavity electrodes, for T1, ER/PR +, no LVI, unifocal, -ve margins, ≥50 years.

units.title: Hormonal Therapy
units.guide: Either ER or PR +ve qualifies. Pre-menopausal women take tamoxifen (SERM) 5 years (up to 10) with hot flashes, endometrial hyperplasia and DVT; post-menopausal get letrozole/anastrozole 5-10 years with osteoporosis - baseline DEXA first, vit D3/Ca/bisphosphonate if low. Pause for pregnancy only after 2 full years, stopping 3 months before conception.

units.title: Prognostic Factors
units.guide: Axillary LN status is the single most important prognosticator, replaced by ER/PR status in metastatic disease. Poor disease factors: bigger, higher stage/grade, nodal spread, metaplastic variant, LVI, extensive DCIS, high Ki-67; poor patient factors: young, premenopausal, BRCA, family/prior history, obesity and unfinished treatment.

units.title: Follow up & Treatment Summary
units.guide: Review 3-monthly for 2 years, 6-monthly to 5 years, yearly after; physical exam every visit, mammogram/USG yearly, pelvic USG for tamoxifen endometrium, and S. Ca 15-3 as marker. Early cancer: BCS with SLNB if N0 (mastectomy if BCS C/I), RT after BCS or with +ve nodes, HT if ER/PR +ve, chemo only for high-risk molecular or TNBC/Her2 +ve.

units.title: LABC & Metastatic Disease
units.guide: LABC = T3N1M0 or any T4/N2/N3 (peau d' orange is T4b), treated NACT → surgery → RT, plus HT if ER/PR +ve and a year of trastuzumab if Her2 +ve. Metastatic (M1) disease is palliative; BRCA +ve tumors get Olaparib.

units.title: Metastatic Subtype-directed Therapy
units.guide: ER/PR +ve Her2- metastases: hormonal therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib), switching to chemo, Zoladex or fulvestrant on resistance. TNBC adds pembrolizumab/atezolizumab (PD-L1); Her2 +ve adds trastuzumab, then lapatinib orally for brain mets or IV TDM1 when resistance appears.

units.title: Pregnancy Associated Breast Cancer
units.guide: Cancer during pregnancy or within a year of delivery - ER/PR -ve, aggressive, diagnosed by core biopsy with USG as IOC. Mastectomy in 1st trimester, BCS in 2nd/3rd with RT after delivery; chemo C/I in 1st but safe later; HT and RT C/I in all trimesters.

units.title: Bilateral & Male Breast Carcinoma
units.guide: Bilateral disease is usually BRCA (+) lobular, staged separately when synchronous and treated per the more aggressive side. Male cancer rides on BRCA2 > BRCA1, obesity, Klinefelter, alcohol and cirrhosis, presents as a hard lump, is biopsied and managed exactly like female breast cancer.

units.title: DCIS & Van Nuys
units.guide: DCIS is non invasive: papillary (m/c), cribriform and solid are ER/PR + with clustered microcalcifications, while comedo with necrosis is the aggressive ER/PR -ve lump-former. Image-guided core biopsy diagnoses; simple mastectomy or BCS + RT treats (BCS C/I if extensive calcification), chemo has no role, HT if ER/PR +ve. Van Nuys scores size, margins, grade & necrosis, age (not ER/PR): low avoids RT, intermediate gets RT, high gets mastectomy.

units.title: LCIS
units.guide: LCIS is now a risk marker (1%/year conversion), B/L multicentric, ER/PR +ve, found incidentally and kept under surveillance. It progresses to invasive ductal or lobular cancer; invasive lobular is B/L multicentric (BCS C/D) with E-cadherin loss, Indian/single-file cells, and CDH mutation also drives diffuse gastric cancer.
